analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (11.11.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 38bps to 7521 (+10% YTD) and did not follow through with a second rebound day. SOX fell 40bps and Nvidia fell 5.5% on uncertainty over Jensen's affair, with Nvidia numbers due 17 Nov.
US 10-year yield rose to 4.99% on higher inflation and Waller's comments on a potential +50bps hike in December.
Cross-asset levels: Brent $92 (Ukraine meeting in Abu Dhabi and Iran headlines), Gold $4058, Bitcoin $74k. Cisco and Applied Materials report earnings on 12 Nov.
October core CPI rose +0.3% vs consensus +0.2%, with shelter, medical services and vehicle insurance higher. The Link market implies nearly 70% for 2 hikes by March 2027.

GS expects a second 25bp Fed hike in December and adds a third 25bp hike in March, which could come as early as January. GS still expects inflation to be meaningfully lower by end-2027 as tariff, energy shock and AI price pressures fade, but suspects recent prints will lead most FOMC participants to signal a third hike.

CoreWeave rose 8% post market. Implied 4Q revenue guidance is 3% above the Street, margins 100bps above and capex 22% below. The financing plan adds no further parent-level unsecured debt through 2027, with customer prepayments, OEM financing and operating cash flow as additional levers.

CoreWeave 4-5 year contracts now price at $20-25mn/MW against WholeCo revenue/MW of about $10mn and capex of about $40mn/MW. GS now estimates unlevered IRR of 20-30% before residual value, vs 15-21% prior.
Chinese equities have not converted macro growth into equity returns since 2020, with 6% EPS CAGR since 2021. GS projects 10% trend EPS growth and stays bullish on Stable and Cash Return Growth.

BCG survey on agentic commerce: among AI shoppers, 96% use AI for product discovery and 80% for consideration. 24% use it for purchasing and 4% of consumers would let an AI agent complete a purchase alone.

BTC ETFs saw about $1.3b net outflows last week, pushing YTD cumulative flows negative. BTC reclaimed its 200-dma, and past reclaims after sustained downtrends showed 180-day forward returns of 53% to 61%.

GS TMT spec sales describes strong 3Q earnings, financing visibility, relief in oil and rates, lowered expectations and a positioning reset, with the NDX at 18x-19x forward P/E and up about 10% on the year.

US consumer 2027 outlook: GS expects real income growth to be more evenly distributed, supported by household wealth, and is not concerned by the 3.8% saving rate. It expects consumer spending to grow 2.2% in 2027.

GS likes shorting its Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP, 43 stocks). Earnings and dividend yields are unattractive relative to fixed income, growth is insufficient, revisions are rolling over and valuations are in the 90th percentile relative to the last year.

European datacenter call with EUDCA: development is unaffected by US midterms, the market could more than double by the early 2030s, and power grids are the largest bottleneck. GS points to its European Power Basket (GSXEPOWR, 39 stocks).

GS views the Semis drawdown as overdone. 35 GW of 2027 deployments are largely in progress with low execution risk. NVDA and AVGO are at very attractive entry points, and AMAT and LRCX are particularly compelling.
Russia: more than 400k Russians killed in Ukraine since the 2022 invasion, per leaked state statistics agency data.

Chart of the Day: global memory stocks have historically bottomed around tangible book value. Stat of the Day: Chinese equity market cap rose from US$600bn in 2002 to about US$20tn, and listed companies from 1600 to 7000.
